issues.section: Hands-on: Lab 2 (intro) / Week 1 · Prepare for Week 2
issues.quote: You need Geant4 11.4 and CMake ≥ 3.16 (Week 1, step 7).
issues.problem: No page explains how to install Geant4 11.4 with datasets on any OS; Week 1 step 7 only checks versions. Nothing at all for Windows users, who are the majority in industry.
issues.fix: Add an install item (WSL2 Ubuntu, Linux, macOS, or the container promised on landing.html) with time estimate and a check script; mention it on the course home FAQ.

issues.section: G4Exception before you join / founding pricing
issues.quote: a Linux or macOS machine (container provided for Windows)
issues.problem: No container image exists in the course pages, README or code/; the US$290 tier also promises 'the container image'.
issues.fix: Ship the container (and a Week-2 instruction to use it) or remove the promise.

issues.quote: 09–10 A multi-layer muon telescope, as used in muography
issues.problem: Actual Weeks 9-10 are musrSim and transverse-field μSR, which the course itself calls optional for the muography track. Landing also says 'about five hours a week' vs index '2–3 h a week', and 'basic C++: classes and pointers' vs FAQ 'C++ experience helps'.
issues.fix: Make landing.html match the syllabus, time and prerequisites on index.html.

issues.section: 3 Muons in rock · Scattering: the second effect
issues.quote: Each muon also zig-zags slightly as it passes many nuclei (multiple Coulomb scattering, Week 4).
issues.problem: Week 4 contains no mention of scattering at all (0 matches for 'scatter'); scattering appears only in passing in Weeks 3, 6 and 7.
issues.fix: Point to the right week, or add a multiple-scattering section (Highland formula, angle vs thickness/material) to Week 4.

issues.quote: Most muography telescopes have no magnet, so the momentum of each muon is unknown.
issues.problem: Scattering muography (the mode the primer lists for containers, reinforced concrete, waste drums - and what industry uses for pipes/vessels) is never simulated in any lab. Week 7's two-tracker line fit is exactly the in/out angle measurement of scattering tomography, but the course never says so.
issues.fix: Add an optional Lab 7.3: remove the field, put a steel plate/pipe wall between the trackers, measure the deflection-angle width vs wall thickness, compare with Highland, then a simple PoCA. Mention this in the Week 7 muography note.

issues.quote: Week 10's app is a complete template, with a messenger for pre-initialisation parameters
issues.problem: The capstone template and every Lab 12 example (tf.mac, repro_check with week10) are from Week 10, which the muography track is told is optional. No muography geometry (rock, tunnel, steel) or cosmic energy-spectrum generator exists anywhere in code/.
issues.fix: Provide a muography capstone template: a cos²θ + energy-spectrum generator, a rock or steel object, two tracker stacks, and an exposure-time estimate.

issues.section: Hands-on: Lab 12 · Rehearse the defence with a referee
issues.quote: Ten minutes on the clock. Your partner asks three questions from this list and grades with the weights above
issues.problem: Self-paced students have no partner, peers or evaluator, and no place to submit. The course offers no certificate or proof of completion; progress is 'Only in this browser, on this device' (index FAQ).
issues.fix: Define the self-paced path: submission form or repo link, instructor/TA review, and a certificate with hours and capstone grade; state it on the course home.

issues.section: How each week works / FAQ · How much time does it take?
issues.quote: About 2 to 3 hours a week, about 30 hours in all.
issues.problem: Page totals already reach 3 h (Weeks 5, 9, 10) and 4 h (Week 12), excluding install and debugging. For a C++ newcomer at 3 h/week, Weeks 2, 5 and 7 each take two weeks; realistic is 20-24 calendar weeks.
issues.fix: Publish a part-time schedule (e.g. 'about 45 h; 16-24 weeks at 3 h/week') and mark which lab steps are optional per track.

issues.problem: index.html (and landing.html) have no <meta name=viewport>; on a 390 px phone the course home lays out at 980 px and is shrunk (my screenshot P06-phone-index-top.png). primer and week pages have it. Unsure whether the publishing wrapper adds it; on GitHub Pages it would not.
issues.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to index.html and landing.html.

issues.section: Hands-on: Labs 5.1–5.3 · Run the three configurations
issues.problem: The printout labels a geometric fraction 'eff'; the text then says 'the efficiency is the geometry'. Week 1 MC0003 warns against exactly this naming. An engineer reporting '11% efficiency' to a manager would mislead.
issues.fix: Label it 'fraction of generated muons' and keep 'efficiency' for counter response given a crossing.

issues.problem: 'cos2' here samples c = u^(1/4) (cos² intensity crossing a plane), while Week 1 step 5 'Give it a real sky: the cos²θ sea-level shape' uses u^(1/3). Same name, two samplers.
issues.fix: Add a one-line comment/label: 'cos² intensity through a horizontal plane = cos³ per solid angle (Week 1 step 5)'.
